text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - The December Bund future ended trade on a contract high and an all-time high of 101.70 points. Dealers said that local dealers on London's LIFFE exchange helped boost the Bund future to new highs, even though volumes were low because of the Thanksgiving holiday in the U.S. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.72, up 0.35 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilt futures closed higher, taking their cue from Bunds in the absence of fresh domestic developments but they remain vulnerable to setbacks if further evidence confirms that the economy is powering ahead. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 111-1/32, up 14/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures followed Bunds higher in a calm session with calls for lower rates from within the Bank of France's inner sanctum buoying sentiment despite a jittery franc. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.28, up 0.20 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Debt intruments closed lower but made up a bit of ground after an easier start in a dull session of range-trading, lacking direction from the U.S. with markets there closed. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.88, up 0.02 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - The U.S. Treasury market is closed today for the Thanksgiving holiday. The market will resume on Friday, although trading will be abbreviated in New York when the market will close at 1400 EST/1900 GMT. Treasuries prices ended mostly higher in New York yesterday, with the key 6-1/2 percent 30-year benchmark bond up 6/32 at 100-31/32, yielding 6.43 percent.

JAPAN - The benchmark 182nd Japanese government bond was bought slightly in late afternoon trade after the release of Japanese industrial output data. "The forecasts for the months ahead were considered weak, and slight buying ensued," a trust bank trader said. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 126.29, down 0.05 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The U.S. Thanksgiving holiday kept dollar Eurobonds away, but European currencies provided some business. SBC Warburg lead managed a 100 million mark bond repackaging Russian MinFin bonds. Also from Russia, national power company Unified Energy System and the Nizhny Novgorod region said they were considering Eurobond issues for 1997. Samsung Electronics issued a 300 million mark five-year bond, OKB a 1.0 billion Czech crown two-year deal and Credit Local a 100 million Ecu transaction.
